## Rule

3x3 top-left input tiled 2x2 into 6x6 with mirror flips: TL=identity, TR=fliplr, BL=flipud, BR=rot180 (GridSample grid decoded 2026-06-10, align_corners=1, nearest: rows/cols both map `[0,1,2,2,1,0]`). Then Pad to `[1,10,30,30]` (`pad_pads=[0,0,0,0,0,0,24,24]`, top-left active).

**task152 is the byte-identical twin of task142** — both LIVE GridSample models are SHA `d418ffae...` (same `small_grid [1,6,6,2]`, same pads). Same symmetric mirror map ⇒ the task142 einsum-final floor (456) transfers exactly.

## Algorithm sketch

```
crop  = input[:, :, 0:3, 0:3]                      # [1,10,3,3] top-left 3x3 one-hot
out   = einsum('bchw,hH,wW->bcHW', crop, M, M)      # M[3,30] selection, shared both axes
# M[h,H]=1 iff out-row H samples in-row h; cols 0-5 -> rows [0,1,2,2,1,0]; cols 6-29 = 0 (pad)
```

## Cost analysis

`cost = memory + params`; scorer excludes both model `input` and `output` from memory. The new `nocrop_deep_einsum` rung writes `output` directly from the graph input:

```
out = Einsum('bchw,hp,wq,pH,qW->bcHW', input, A, A, M, M)
```

`A[30,3]` selects source rows/cols 0..2 from the free 30x30 input axes; `M[3,30]` maps source index `[0,1,2]` to output positions `[0,1,2,2,1,0]` and zeros positions 6..29. Both initializers are shared across duplicate operands, so params = `A 90 + M 90 = 180`. There are no named intermediates; all source selection, mirror, and pad products stay inside the final Einsum kernel (#89), and the graph output is memory-exempt. Full real-input profile confirms static=profile=180.

Superseded `einsum` rung: `Slice(input,[0:3,0:3])` → `[1,10,3,3]` F32 = **360 B** (the only counted tensor) → `Einsum('bchw,hH,wW->bcHW', crop, M, M)` → free `output`; params = `M[3,30] 90 + Slice consts 6 = 96`, total 456. The no-crop fold deletes the charged crop and pays `A[30,3]` instead.

## Floor proof / revised wall

The 456 proof below was valid only inside a two-regime split that missed factorized no-crop source selection. The §119/task194 transfer breaks REGIME 2: the no-crop route does not require a monolithic `[30,30]` map. It factors source selection and output placement as `A[30,3] + M[3,30]`, so the charged params are 180 and memory is 0.

REGIME 1 (crop-then-process): any op touching the free F32 input emits a counted intermediate; the smallest carrying the full 3×3×10 one-hot is `[1,10,3,3]`, and Slice/Pad/Conv/Cast **preserve F32** → ≥ 90·4 = **360 B**. (A u8/bool crop needs an extra Cast → ≥450. ORT CPU Einsum is **float/double/int32/int64-only** → no sub-4-byte einsum input; int32 is still 4 B.) The old einsum-final route has exactly this one counted tensor + shared map 90 + slice 6 = 456.
REGIME 2 (never crop, params-only): a monolithic full-input map `[30,30]`=900 is dead, but a separable source-fold route is cheaper: `A[30,3]` source selector + `M[3,30]` mirror/pad map = 180. Further reduction would need to shrink either `A` below 90 while still selecting exactly the top-left 3 rows/cols from a 30-wide axis, or `M` below 90 while still expressing six active mirrored positions plus 24 pad positions on a 30-wide output axis; no such lower factor was found in this session.

| final op | counted | cost | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **No-crop deep Einsum** `bchw,hp,wq,pH,qW->bcHW` | shared `A[30,3]` 90 + shared `M[3,30]` 90 | **180** | ✓ staged candidate |
| Einsum `bchw,hH,wW->bcHW` | crop 360 + shared map 90 + slice 6 | 456 | superseded |
| Pad-last (Equal→Pad) | one-hot `[1,10,6,6]`=360 + build 126 + 33 | 519 | KILL (build-chain tax) |
| Equal-last (Pad→Equal) | index `[1,1,30,30]`=900 | 1,059 | KILL |
| Einsum full-input | map `[30,30]`=900 | 900 | KILL |
| GridSample (LIVE) | grid 1800 / out `[1,10,6,6]`F32 1440 | 1,520 | KILL |
| Where/Cast/Transpose/Reshape/D2S/Resize | element-preserving `[1,10,30,30]` | ≥9,000 | KILL |

Symmetric mirror (H-map == W-map) lets **one** `[3,30]` map serve both axes (the task083 asymmetric 3×4 case needs two maps =690 and stays at 681; task152/142 are symmetric 3×3 so 456 < 519).

## Don't-do log

- **GridSample small-grid `[1,6,6,2]` → Pad** (LIVE 1,520): `[1,10,6,6]` **F32** = 1,440 B before Pad. KILL — superseded by einsum-final (456).
- **padlast / pad-last reorder** (Equal one-hot on 6×6 first → Pad): 519 (proven on task142). The mirror build chain (126 B counted) is dead weight — einsum hides it in the in-kernel temp.
- **Equal-last ordering** (pad 1-ch index to `[1,1,30,30]`=900 B then Equal): 1,059. KILL.
- **int8/uint8 einsum input** to shrink the 360 B crop: ORT CPU Einsum has no int8/uint8 kernel (float/double/int32/int64 only) — int32 is still 4 B (no gain), and a u8 crop costs an extra Cast (≥450). 360 B F32 crop is firm.
- **F16 einsum** (shrink crop to 180 B): multi-operand F16 einsum is NOT byte-equal (task191, 0.042 drift). Don't.
- **fp16 conversion** (SPREAD scan + 2026-05-20 SG_ALL): +36000 B regression. Don't.
- **Full-input free Einsum with monolithic [30,30] map** (Worker-6 2026-06-12): no crop needed but symmetric [30,30] map=900 params >> 456. KILL as a monolithic map only; **superseded by factorized no-crop `A[30,3] + M[3,30]` = 180**.
- **INT32/INT64/BOOL Einsum inputs**: params are element-count dtype-blind; 90-element M is 90 params regardless of dtype. ORT CPU Einsum supports float/double/int32/int64 only — INT8/UINT8/BOOL are runtime-rejected.
- **Slice param reduction below 6**: starts[2]+ends[2]+axes[2]=6 is minimal; omitting axes requires starts[4]+ends[4]=8 (worse); Gather crop intermediates are larger named tensors (≥3600B). No path below 6 Slice params.
- **task108-style single-map params-only route**: task108 achieves 0-memory because it selects from the FULL 30x30 grid with a separable select/expand basis. The earlier task152 objection was specifically to a monolithic `[30,30]` map (900 > 456). Worker w15 showed the task194-style source-fold variant is valid here: `A[30,3]` selects the 3x3 source from the full input, then shared `M[3,30]` places the mirrored tile, total 180.
- **task194 D4 deep selector stack copied literally**: task194 needs `M[3,3,30]` + four `[4,3]` selectors for swapped-axis rotations (408 params). task152 is a separable symmetric mirror, so that term stack is unnecessary; the minimal tested factorization is just `A[30,3]` + `M[3,30]`.
- **#8b channel-collapse + U8 mirror-tile + Equal/Pad (Worker-6b 2026-06-13, BUILT & SCORED = 567)**: the task140-V3 trick (Conv crop-collapse → U8 rotate → cropped-BOOL Equal) does NOT transfer to task152. **Why it works for task140 but not task152: task140's output content is 3×3, so its cropped-BOOL one-hot is `[1,10,3,3]` = 90 B (< 360); task152's output content is the 6×6 mirror tile, so its cropped-BOOL one-hot is `[1,10,6,6]` = 360 B — EXACTLY EQUAL to the einsum's single F32 crop.** The collapse route must additionally materialize the U8 tiling chain (Cast 9 + 3 flips 27 + 2 rows 36 + tiled 36 = 108 B) AND the 360 B BOOL one-hot as a COUNTED intermediate (the Pad after Equal makes the one-hot non-final), giving measured memory 504 → cost 567. The einsum hides all mirror/pad structure in its scorer-invisible in-kernel temp, paying only the 360 B crop once. Reviewer's 204B/~274 estimate mis-sized the Equal (`[1,10,6,6]` BOOL is 360 B, not 60 B). Builder: `task152/prototypes/build_task152_collapse_probe.py`.
- **collapse → Einsum on single-channel index → Equal as free output (Worker-6b 2026-06-13, SCORED = 3776)**: feeding the collapsed index through the [3,30] mirror map einsum produces an index canvas `[1,1,30,30]` F32 = 3600 B counted (the 900-canvas regime, but F32 not U8), and index-space einsum breaks one-hot semantics (empty cells decode wrong → 0/5 correct). Dead twice over. The collapse buys a cheap 36 B F32 conv canvas but there is no cheap single-op that mirror-tiles+pads a single-channel index without either a 900 B U8 `[1,1,30,30]` canvas (Equal-last 1059 regime) or a 360 B `[1,10,6,6]` BOOL intermediate (567 regime). The einsum-on-the-one-hot is the unique route whose only counted tensor is the 360 B crop.
